newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia natgas pipeline ruptured, supplies cut.
newsitem.headline: Colombia natgas pipeline ruptured, supplies cut.

text.p: One of Colombia's main gas pipelines was ruptured Monday, hitting 2 million domestic consumers in the capital Bogota, a spokesman for the state-run oil company Ecopetrol said.

He said the pipeline, which transports 9.3 million cubic feet of natural gas per day, was broken at a point known as Puente Quetame on the route between the city of Villavicencio, in eastern Meta province, and Bogota.
The spokesman said it was unclear whether the pipeline had been dynamited by leftist rebels operating in the region or whether it had been destroyed by a landslide.
All the homes affected were in working class districts of south and southwest Bogota. It was not known how long it would take to repair the damage, the Ecopetrol spokesman said.
